chapter_theme: The closing summary of the whole work (நூற் கட்டுரை): one sentence says that within the Tamil land bounded by Kumari, Venkatam and the two seas, the Silappathikaram gathers the matter of akam and puram, the three aims of virtue, wealth and pleasure for humans and gods alike, song, the lute, melody, rhythm, the stage and dance, the vari, the kuravai and the other forms, and makes its meaning plain as a good mirror shows a tall hill, its story's matter being completed in Manimekalai.

silappathikaram:nool_katturai:1-18.reading: The narrator closes the epic by saying that, in the cool Tamil country bounded by Kumari, Venkatam and the eastern and western seas, with its two kinds of Tamil, the work joins the virtue, wealth and pleasure of the five landscapes, fitting for humans and gods alike, to conduct that keeps the tradition, sets the meaning that rises from words in faultless metre as akam and puram, gathers song, the lute, melody, rhythm, the stage, its rules and dance, and the vari, kuravai and other forms, and lays out its intent as a good mirror shows a vast hill, being the Silappathikaram whose story's matter is completed in Manimekalai.
silappathikaram:nool_katturai:1-18.nuance: The close describes the work by its land, its language and its arts, and not by the three morals the patikam announced at 0:55-57: karma, the pathini and the death of the king who erred are not named here, and aram appears only as the first of the three aims of poetry's matter (line 4). Lines 5 and 6 claim the epic's matter is valid for gods as well as humans, which fits a story that ends with Kannaki's ascent and her worship. The simile of lines 15 and 16 claims that a large matter is shown whole in a small compass, as a mirror holds a hill. மணிமேகலைமேல் உரைப்பொருள் முற்றிய (line 17) can be read as the story's matter being completed in the work Manimekalai or upon the person Manimekalai, Kovalan and Madhavi's daughter; either way the line declares the epic's story unfinished within its own covers, and the reading here does not choose between the two.

links.note: The patikam's opening frame names three morals the poem will show (dharma as death to the erring king, the praise of the pathini, the past deed that comes to fruit) and calls the poem a பாட்டுடைச் செய்யுள்; the closing summary describes the finished work by its land, its akam and puram matter, its three aims and its music, dance and song forms, and repeats none of the morals.
links.teaches: The two frames of the epic describe it in different terms, the opening as a story built to prove three moral claims and the close as a compendium of Tamil poetics, music and dance, so the work presents itself at the start as an argument and at the end as an art, and the morals are left for the story itself to carry.

links.note: The Silappathikaram's last line calls it the work whose story's matter is completed in Manimekalai; the Manimekalai patikam closes by saying that Saathan set out Manimekalai's renunciation (மணிமேகலை துறவு) in thirty songs, with Ilango hearing it, reversing the Silappathikaram patikam, where Ilango sang and Saathan heard.
links.teaches: Each work's frame names the other's author as its listener, and the Silappathikaram declares its own story finished only in a sequel whose subject is a daughter's renunciation, so the pair presents the two epics as one story whose tale of justice and chastity reaches its end in the turn from household life to the robe.

source_issues: The edition's printed numbering ends at line 15 while the summary has 18 lines as cut; the printed numbers may count the short lines or the closing colophon differently.
Line 18 (சிலப்பதி காரம் முற்றும்) is a colophon that also completes the sentence (முற்றிய in line 17 governs it), so it is marked as part of the unit.
